The must-sees

8 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Square

    Augustusplatz

    The square was a major gathering point of the peaceful demonstrations of autumn 1989. Its buildings span from GDR modernism to the new university hall.

    Look for

    The pointed glass gable of the university’s Paulinum recalls the church that once stood on that spot.

  2. 02
    Culture · 1981

    Gewandhaus

    The orchestra goes back to 1743 and takes its name from the cloth merchants’ hall where it first played. Felix Mendelssohn was one of its conductors; the present hall opened in 1981.

    Look for

    The ceiling painting seen through the glass is Sighard Gille’s Song of Life.

  3. 03
    Station · 1915

    Leipzig Central Station

    Completed in 1915, it is one of the largest terminal stations in Europe by area. Its two great halls were once run by the Prussian and Saxon railways.

    Look for

    Along one of the platforms, a museum track keeps historic locomotives on display.

  4. 04
    Landmark · 1913

    Monument to the Battle of the Nations

    It was unveiled in 1913, a hundred years after the battle in which allied armies defeated Napoleon near Leipzig. A platform at the top looks out over the whole city.

    Look for

    Down in the crypt, giant stone warriors with bowed heads stand guard over the fallen.

  5. 05
    Shopping

    Mädler Passage

    The arcade was built in the 1910s on the site of an old trade hall. Goethe used Auerbachs Keller as a scene in his Faust, and bronze figures from the play stand at its stairs.

    Look for

    In the rotunda, a glockenspiel with bells of Meissen porcelain chimes over the shoppers.

  6. 06
    Building

    Old Town Hall

    It was built in the 1550s under Hieronymus Lotter, reportedly in less than a year. It now houses the museum of city history.

    Look for

    Behind the town hall, on the Naschmarkt, a statue of the young Goethe recalls his student years in Leipzig.

  7. 07
    Church

    St. Nicholas Church

    Monday peace prayers held here in the 1980s grew into the Monday demonstrations of 1989. On 9 October that year about 70,000 people marched peacefully around the ring road.

    Look for

    In the churchyard outside stands a copy of one of the palm-topped columns, set up as a memorial to the protests of 1989.

  8. 08
    Church

    St. Thomas Church

    Johann Sebastian Bach was cantor here from 1723 until his death in 1750, and his grave is in front of the altar. The St. Thomas Boys Choir still sings here every week.

    Look for

    On the Bach statue outside, the left coat pocket is turned inside out, said to show how little money he had.
